newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end mixed on pre-report positioning.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end mixed on pre-report positioning.

text.p: CBOT soybeans ended mixed Wednesday following a session of choppy price action as traders exited positions before the upcoming holiday weekend and Monday's acreage report, traders said.
""It was just very nervous trade," a floor source said. "We've got the report following a three-day weekend. No one's really comfortable establishing new positions."

The U.S. Department of Agriculture will release planted acreage forecasts for 1997 and quarterly grain stocks data on Monday at 0730 CST/1330 GMT. Trading typically slows in front reports and holidays.
The CBOT will be closed Friday in observance of Good Friday.
The market found some support from talk China was seeking soybeans from the U.S. for spot delivery because of long loading delays at South American ports, traders said.
"We're like a convenience store for other nations," said one floor trader. "They'll pay the higher prices because we can guarantee delivery."
CBOT soybeans settled down one to up two cents per bushel, with May down one at $8.41 and July up 1/2 at $8.44-1/2.
Loading delays at South American ports can stretch as long as 50 days, U.S. traders said.
On the day, Griffin Trading sold 3 million bushels May and 1.5 million November. Refco bought one bushels May and crushers were late buyers of soybeans, floor sources said.
In options trading, Produce Grain bought 400 $8.00 May puts and Cargill Investor Services bought 400 May $8.25 puts, floor sources said.
Volume was estimated by the CBOT at 40,000 contracts, compared with Monday's actual volume of 45,782 contracts.
